stories.title: Design-token lock-down: the shared token set every Frontstage and Project Room surface is built from

acceptance_criteria.text: A single token source of truth exists (CSS custom properties, surfaced to Tailwind through its theme configuration) covering every category PRD §12.2 names before page creation may expand: one display/serif family and one sans/utility family; at most three approved font combinations; colour palette; type scale; line heights; text measures; spacing scale; gallery gaps; radii; overlay and vignette presets; breakpoints; animation timing. Every value is a named step in a limited scale — no one-off values — and the file carries the CLAUDE.md structured metadata header. A test asserts every one of the twelve categories is present and non-empty.

The typefaces are **Fraunces** (display serif, headlines) and **Inter** (body/UI sans), per the creative brief confirmed in `po-requests.md` item 9, self-hosted from the repository with no external font request. A test asserts the built CSS and any layout head contain no request to `fonts.googleapis.com` or `fonts.gstatic.com`, that both families are declared with `font-display: swap`, and that the primary weights are preloaded so no font swap causes layout shift.

The palette is near-black ink (deliberately not pure `#000`), a neutral grey scale for secondary/tertiary content and surfaces, and **no accent colour** beyond that range — the confirmed brief. A test computes the WCAG contrast ratio from the token values themselves for every ink-on-surface pair the token set declares as a usable combination, and fails any pair below AA (4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text and non-text indicators).

The existing US-8 public shell is rewired onto the tokens: `src/components/layout/PublicShell.tsx`, `VerticalMenu.tsx`, `SiteFooter.tsx`, `MobileMenuTrigger.tsx` and `src/app/(frontend)/layout.tsx` use only token references. A test asserts no raw hex colour, no raw `px` font-size, and no arbitrary Tailwind bracket value remains in those five files. Rendered output is unchanged in structure — this is a re-parameterisation, not a redesign — proven by a DOM/structural snapshot of each of the five files' rendered output taken before and after the rewire, asserted identical (class-list token substitutions aside).

An internal `noindex` token-specimen route renders the full set for human confirmation: the type scale at every step with both families, the palette with its computed contrast ratios shown, the spacing scale, radii, gallery gaps, and each overlay/vignette preset over a sample photograph. stories.title: Gallery Placement: a Frontstage page renders a Backstage gallery through the agreed API boundary

acceptance_criteria.text: A Payload `GalleryPlacement` model exists with exactly the fields PRD §14 specifies: the Backstage gallery identifier (the gallery `slug`, stored as a plain external-identifier field), layout (`slideshow` or `masonry`), optional heading, optional description, optional theme/overlay preset drawn from the US-23 token presets, visibility rules, and order within the page or story. A test asserts the model holds **no** foreign key or relation into `backstage-db` — `PAYLOAD_PICPEAK_API_CONTRACT.md`'s "No cross-database access" rule and Reminder 4 both forbid it.

A single server-side Backstage client implements Flow A rows 1–2 of `PAYLOAD_PICPEAK_API_CONTRACT.md`: `GET /api/gallery/:slug/info` for display metadata, then the `POST /api/auth/gallery/verify` handshake followed by `GET /api/gallery/:slug/photos` for the photo list — the handshake is coded even for public galleries, because the contract does not let Frontstage assume `requires_password: false` in advance. Every call carries an explicit timeout. Proven live against the running Backstage stack for a published gallery, reproduced rather than run once.

The existing gallery components under `src/components/gallery/` render the Backstage-sourced photo list unchanged in location, through a new `backstageGalleryMapper` that takes the place of `payloadGalleryMapper.ts` as the data source. This is the "Kept as a Frontstage renderer" disposition `PIVOT_AUDIT.md`'s superseded-artifact table already records. A test asserts no second gallery-rendering component set is introduced.

Caching obeys the contract exactly: the bounded 60-second safety-net cap, display data only, and never a Backstage database row stored Frontstage-side. A test asserts the cached shape contains only the fields the contract's "What the Frontstage is allowed to cache" section permits — rendered image URLs, thumbnails, gallery title/cover, item counts — and that a Frontstage cache is never treated as authoritative.

An internal `noindex` route renders one and the same Backstage gallery through two placements — one `masonry`, one `slideshow` — proving PRD §14's core claim that layout is a placement concern and one gallery can appear in different layouts without the underlying gallery changing. Masonry preserves every received aspect ratio and the photographer's order, never crops or stretches, and reserves aspect-ratio space before load (PRD §15.1); slideshow preloads only current and next (PRD §15.2). A test asserts zero image-caused layout shift on the masonry route; a second test asserts the masonry route's rendered image order and each image's rendered aspect ratio match the photo list returned by `GET /api/gallery/:slug/photos` exactly, with no `object-fit: cover`/crop applied; a third test asserts the slideshow route's network requests show only the current and next image's assets loaded, never the full set.

Failure behaviour is defined and proven: an unreachable Backstage, a timeout, or a 404 slug renders the page with a placeholder for that placement and a logged error — never a 500 on a public page, and never a partially rendered gallery presented as complete. Tested by pointing a placement at a slug that does not exist and by simulating a Backstage timeout.

acceptance_criteria.text: A Frontstage receiver route accepts the Backstage webhook and recomputes the `X-PicPeak-Signature` HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body **before** trusting any field in it. An absent, malformed, or mismatched signature is rejected with 401 and revalidates nothing. A test proves a forged body with a stale signature is rejected. `PAYLOAD_PICPEAK_API_CONTRACT.md` Flow C step 3 states this rule and it is the whole security basis of the flow.

The receiver extracts the changed gallery's `id`/`slug` from the verified payload, maps it to the `GalleryPlacement` records referencing that slug, and calls the existing on-demand revalidation mechanism in `src/lib/galleryRevalidation.ts` — re-keyed from its current Payload-gallery-title lookup (`getGalleryBearingPaths`) to a Backstage slug lookup. The mechanism's role is unchanged; only the source of truth it maps from has changed with the pivot. The fixed event catalog it handles (`event.published`, `photo.uploaded`, `photo.deleted`) is asserted against contract row 5, and an unrecognised event type is accepted with 2xx and ignored, not treated as an error.

The receiver returns 2xx promptly after queuing or performing the revalidation, not after Backstage's own work finishes — contract row 5's requirement. A test asserts the response is returned without waiting on the revalidation's completion.

The live-proof harness's connective tissue is stood up once and recorded, so AC-26.4.1.2, AC-26.4.1.3, AC-26.4.2 and AC-26.4.3 all reuse it instead of rebuilding it. A new `WEBHOOK_LIVE_PROOF.md` at the repository root opens with sections (a)-(c), recorded as verbatim commands and their real output in the sprint-3 evidence style: (a) the Frontstage app and the Backstage stack running together on the shared Docker Compose `default` network, shown through `docker compose --profile webprod --profile backstage ps` and the Frontstage container's network aliases; (b) a webhook subscription registered through `POST /api/admin/webhooks` whose URL reaches the AC-26.1 receiver by its Compose service hostname (`http://web:3000/api/webhooks/picpeak`) and whose `events` array lists all three types this story handles (`event.published`, `photo.uploaded`, `photo.deleted`); and (c) the secret reconciliation this criterion owns and must settle. Upstream issues a `whsec_...` secret per subscription and returns it in plaintext exactly once, at creation (`adminWebhooks.js:75-142`; every later read returns only `secret_preview`), while the AC-26.1 receiver verifies against a single `PICPEAK_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. Record the rule that resolves this — one subscription, its secret captured at the create call, written to `.env` as `PICPEAK_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, the Frontstage container recreated — and record that re-registering the subscription rotates the secret and silently breaks the receiver until the new value is applied, so the harness must never be blindly re-created.

The criterion closes on a live check that needs no gallery and no publish: from inside the `backstage-backend` container, a POST to the receiver's Compose-hostname URL with an unsigned body returns 401 — an answer only the AC-26.1 receiver can produce, so it proves the network path and the signature gate at once, and a DNS or routing failure looks nothing like it — and the same POST signed with the reconciled secret returns 200. Both commands and both responses are recorded.

Fixed scope, so no session spends its budget rediscovering what sprint 3 already established: `PIVOT_AUDIT.md`'s AC-17.7 write-up already proves this Backstage-side path live at the pinned commit and its commands are reusable verbatim. Upstream's `validateExternalUrl` (`networkValidation.js:85-95`) rejects loopback and private-range addresses and hostnames ending `.internal`/`.local`/`.localhost`, so a bare Compose service name passes and `localhost` will not — this is why the receiver URL must be the service hostname. An uncommitted `scripts/webhook-live-proof-setup.sh` from a prior session already performs (a)-(c) idempotently and is the starting point; it has never been run to completion, so its output is the thing under proof here, not evidence that already exists.

Reusing the harness AC-26.4.1.1 recorded, without rebuilding it, the fixtures the publish proof acts on are created and recorded as section (d) of `WEBHOOK_LIVE_PROOF.md`, again as verbatim commands and their real output: two draft Backstage galleries created through `POST /api/admin/events` with `is_draft: true`; a Payload `gallery-placements` record for each, pointing at that gallery's slug; and the named Frontstage page that renders those placements, shown live serving its pre-publish state (both galleries are drafts, so it renders them as unavailable). Nothing is published in this criterion — the publish is AC-26.4.1.3's to prove.

Fixed scope, so this stays assembly rather than investigation: `is_draft: true` rather than `false` precisely so the publish under proof is a real state transition — the same route with `is_draft: false` fires `event.created` (`adminEvents.js:761-784`) and `event.published` (`adminEvents.js:823-830`) inside the create call, collapsing the thing being proven into setup. Two galleries rather than one because the pinned fork's publish route is a one-way draft->live transition (`adminEvents.js:1049` 400s "Event is already published" on a second call) and ships no un-publish route, so AC-26.4.1.3's reproduction run needs a second, independently created draft rather than a database edit underneath the first. Upstream derives the slug from `event_name` + `event_date` and does not accept a slug directly, so each created gallery is read back by slug to confirm it is the one the rest of the harness names. `POST /api/admin/events` also 500s with `EACCES: permission denied, mkdir '/storage'` on a freshly recreated `backstage-backend` container; the one-time operational fix (`mkdir -p /storage && chown -R nodejs:nodejs /storage` inside the container) is already recorded in `PIVOT_AUDIT.md` under AC-17.5.1 and AC-17.7 and must simply be re-applied and recorded — it is a known upstream defect already raised, not a new investigation. An uncommitted `scripts/webhook-live-proof-setup.sh` and a `/dev/gallery-webhook-proof` page from a prior session already cover this ground and are the starting point.

Before any publish is made, the read-only observation machinery `scripts/ac26.4.1-live-proof.sh` depends on is proven to work against the running stack, and recorded as section (e)(i) of `WEBHOOK_LIVE_PROOF.md` as verbatim commands and their real output. Every step here is read-only and repeatable: the Backstage admin login; the subscription id resolved from the receiver URL `http://web:3000/api/webhooks/picpeak` rather than hardcoded; the numeric Backstage event id resolved from each of the two proof slugs, shown with `is_draft: true` still true for both; the served page at `/dev/gallery-webhook-proof` shown returning `unavailable` for both slugs through the script's own `page_state` extraction, recorded together with the response's cache headers; and the delivery read-back path exercised end to end — `GET /api/admin/webhooks/:id/deliveries` listed, then one row read back through `GET /api/admin/webhooks/:id/deliveries/:deliveryId` to show the detail route does return a `payload` a gallery slug can be matched inside.

Fixed scope, and this criterion publishes nothing. It exists because the publish it precedes is one-way: the pinned fork's publish route 400s "Event is already published" on a second call (`adminEvents.js:1049`) and ships no un-publish route, so a parsing or lookup bug discovered *during* the publish run consumes a fixture that can only be replaced by deleting and recreating the gallery. Proving the read-only half first costs no fixture and removes that risk. Two facts already recorded live make specific checks necessary rather than optional: section (d) recorded the proof page served with `x-nextjs-cache: HIT` and `x-nextjs-stale-time: 300` despite the route's own `export const revalidate = 60`, so record what the page actually serves now rather than assuming a 60-second settle; and the delivery *list* route selects a fixed column set that excludes `payload` (`adminWebhooks.js:283-325`), which is the entire reason the detail read-back exists and must be shown working. Where a step's real output differs from what the committed script expects, correct the script and record the correction — that is this criterion's deliverable, not a blocker. Close by recording the fixture-reset procedure AC-26.4.1.2 already established (`DELETE /api/admin/events/:id` on both galleries, then re-run `scripts/webhook-live-proof-setup.sh`) as the named recovery the two criteria after this one use if a publish run fails partway.

The delivery worker polls on its own schedule every `WEBHOOK_DELIVERY_INTERVAL_MS`, default 5000ms (`webhookDeliveryWorker.js:7`), so no manual trigger exists or is needed — there is only waiting. Reproduction against the second gallery belongs to AC-26.4.1.3.3 and is explicitly not this criterion's work; do not run the script's `all` mode. If the run fails partway and consumes the first gallery, reset both fixtures through the procedure AC-26.4.1.3.1 recorded, re-run, and record the reset — a documented reset-and-re-run is a finding, not a failure of this criterion.

The sequence AC-26.4.1.3.2 recorded is re-run against the **second** draft gallery, from those recorded commands and without modifying them, and shown to reproduce — the same three pieces of evidence: the publish, the `event.published` delivery for that gallery reaching `status: success`, and the served Frontstage placement page changing inside the same sub-60-second deadline. Fixed scope: this is `scripts/ac26.4.1-live-proof.sh reproduce`, the invocation the script already splits out for exactly this purpose. A second gallery rather than the first one re-published because the pinned fork's publish route is a one-way draft→live transition (`adminEvents.js:1049`) with no un-publish route, so reproducing through the supported interface needs an independently created draft rather than a database edit underneath the first — AC-26.4.1.2 created it for precisely this. The sequence is re-run and shown to reproduce.

The complete set of `webhookService.fire('photo.uploaded', ...)` call sites in the fork is exactly five — `services/photoProcessor.js:246`, `services/photoProcessor.js:494`, `services/fileWatcher.js:142`, `services/s3AutoImporter.js:144`, `routes/v1/events.js:595` — and the task is to determine which of those five the admin upload path reaches, a choice from a closed list. If the admin upload path reaches none of them, that is a recorded finding and not a blocker: state it plainly in `WEBHOOK_LIVE_PROOF.md` with file and line, satisfy this criterion through whichever of the five listed paths does fire `photo.uploaded` for a photo landing in a published gallery, and raise the gap for the Product Owner the way sprint 3 raised its upstream defects. Today the raw-HTML homepage editor is held off only by a settings default with no server-side flag behind it, so a single `PUT /api/admin/settings/general` write can turn Backstage into a second publisher of the site's `/` route — the duplicate `AC-18.5` identified. The "Public Site" raw HTML/CSS panel in `frontend/src/pages/admin/CMSPage.tsx` is hidden behind the same flag using the fork's existing `RequireFeature` gate, the way the quotes UI already is — so the capability is not merely unreachable at the server, it is not offered. Pillar 3 forbids page-level CSS editing and Payload owns Frontstage publishing; an editor that exists will eventually be used. A test asserts `CMSPage.tsx` does not render the Public Site panel when the `publicSite` flag is false, mirroring the existing test pattern that covers the quotes panel's `RequireFeature` gate.

The deviation is recorded in `FORK_CHANGELOG.md` and `PICPEAK_PORT_LEDGER.md` with the file paths touched, and `UPSTREAM_SYNC.md` names the resulting merge-conflict risk on the next upstream sync.

acceptance_criteria.text: The two representative pages `R2_STORAGE_AND_DELIVERY_ADR.md`'s "Measurements that will decide it" section names — "a portfolio gallery page and a blog gallery page" — exist as internal `noindex` routes and are proven to render real Backstage gallery imagery, because a benchmark page that silently falls back to `GalleryUnavailablePlaceholder` measures nothing. Drafted-but-uncommitted work from the session that hit the turn cap on 2026-08-08 (`logs/20260808_170055_dev-team.json`, `terminal_reason: max_turns`) is already on disk and is the starting point, not a blank page: `src/lib/benchmarkPages.ts` (the two path constants, kept as one source of truth the way `galleryRevalidation.ts`'s placement constants are), `src/app/(frontend)/dev/benchmark-portfolio-gallery/page.tsx` (an all-at-once `GalleryMasonryLayout`) and `src/app/(frontend)/dev/benchmark-story-gallery/page.tsx` (narrative copy wrapped around a `GallerySlideshowLayout`), both resolving through `resolveGalleryPlacementImages(PLACEMENT_DEMO_GALLERY_SLUG)` on the US-25 Flow A path. Review, correct and commit them. The closing criterion is the render proof, not the files' existence: with the Backstage stack up and the US-25 placement gallery seeded, an actual HTTP fetch of each of the two routes returns HTML carrying more than one gallery `` and no placeholder output. The harness output already on disk (`scripts/benchmark/results/run-2026-08-08T13-2*.json`) recorded `imageRequestCount: 1` on both pages — the site logo alone, with an identical LCP on two structurally different pages — and is the exact false-green this criterion exists to prevent. Evidence: the fetched HTML of both routes and the seeding command used are saved under `scripts/benchmark/results/`, plus a Jest suite asserting each page renders the resolved images and never substitutes the placeholder on the `ok` path. No Docker image is built and no Lighthouse run is performed in this criterion.

The four measurements the ADR commits to are extracted from a single Lighthouse result and aggregated across runs by pure logic that needs neither Chrome nor a container image — this criterion builds nothing and runs no browser, so it is verifiable by a plain `docker compose run --rm web npx jest` invocation. Drafted-but-uncommitted work from the same timed-out session is the starting point: `src/lib/benchmark/types.ts`, `src/lib/benchmark/extractMeasurements.ts`, `src/lib/benchmark/aggregateRuns.ts` and `src/lib/benchmark/runHarness.ts`. Each of the four measurements maps to a named Lighthouse audit id and every mapping is asserted rather than assumed: mobile performance score from `categories.performance.score`; image-attributable CLS from the `layout-shifts` audit's per-item `score` summed over items whose node is an image, with the total `cumulative-layout-shift` retained beside it so the image-attributable share is visibly a share; LCP from `largest-contentful-paint.numericValue` under Lighthouse's default mobile simulated throttle, with the throttle settings written into the report rather than left implicit; and the network-payload audit from `network-requests` plus `image-size-responsive`, reporting per-image requested resolution and transfer bytes and flagging any oversized fetch, since the ADR target is "public pages never request full-resolution originals unnecessarily". Reproducibility is enforced in code, not by convention: `runHarness` refuses a `runsPerPage` below `MIN_RUNS_PER_PAGE` with an error naming "a single run is not a measurement", retains every raw run beside the aggregate so the numbers can be re-derived rather than trusted (AC-29.3), and reports median/min/max per metric. Evidence: a green Jest suite driven by a checked-in Lighthouse-result fixture under `src/__tests__/__fixtures__/`; the fixture may be hand-authored to the minimal LHR subset, and each audit id and field name it uses is cited to the `lighthouse` package's own audit source (`core/audits/layout-shifts.js`, `core/audits/network-requests.js`, `core/audits/image-size-responsive.js`), so the mapping is checkable without running Chrome.

The harness runs in Docker from one committed command and is shown to reproduce. `scripts/benchmark/Dockerfile`, `scripts/benchmark/package.json`, `scripts/benchmark/package-lock.json` and `scripts/benchmark/run.ts` are already drafted on disk, but the services their docblocks reference do not exist — `docker-compose.yml` on `main` declares only `web`, `db`, `backstage-db`, `backstage-backend`, `backstage-frontend`, `mailhog` and `webhook-receiver`, with no `lighthouse-benchmark` service and no app service for it to target, which is why nobody but the original session could run this. Add the missing service(s) to `docker-compose.yml`, reaching the app by Docker-network hostname and never `localhost` (CLAUDE.md Docker Rules), with `scripts/benchmark/results/` bind-mounted so output survives the container, and record the single command as a named section in `BACKSTAGE_STARTUP.md`. Evidence, and this is what "shown to reproduce" means concretely: that one command is run twice back to back against the same build and the same seeded gallery from AC-29.1.1; both timestamped machine-readable JSON reports are committed under `scripts/benchmark/results/`; and a short reproducibility note committed beside them states, per page and per metric, the spread between the two invocations' medians. That stated spread is the noise floor AC-29.3's pass/fail against the ADR's "near ninety" and "around two and a half seconds" targets must be read against — a target missed by less than the spread is not a miss. The three `run-2026-08-08T13-2*.json` files already on disk were taken before the pages rendered any gallery imagery; they are superseded and are deleted rather than committed.

A bounded mechanism map for candidate paths 1 and 2, written **before** either is measured, because the unsplit AC-29.2's premise that 'both mechanisms already exist in the pinned fork' is only half true and sending a session to measure path 2 without checking that first is what timed it out twice. This criterion runs no browser, builds no image and measures nothing; it reads named fork files and records what it finds as a new `### Candidate mechanism map (AC-29.2.1)` subsection of `R2_STORAGE_AND_DELIVERY_ADR.md`, placed above the existing `### Measurements that will decide it`. The searches are pre-run here so this is confirmation work, not discovery, and each claim below is to be verified at the pinned commit rather than trusted. **Path 1 (serve through the Backstage) already holds and is already what the harness measured**: `GET /api/gallery/:slug/photos` builds `thumbnail_url`, `hero_url` and `preview_url` as backend-served routes at `vendor/picpeak/backend/src/routes/gallery.js:516-525`, `src/components/gallery/backstageGalleryMapper.ts` maps those three onto the Gallery Engine's thumbnail/medium/large tiers, and `src/components/gallery/galleryImageLoader.ts` picks among them — so the AC-29.1.3 runs already committed under `scripts/benchmark/results/` are path-1 numbers. Record explicitly whether they may be cited as path 1's measurement or must be re-run under a path label; that answer is what AC-29.2.2 acts on. Note that the ADR's own wording points path 1 at `protectedImages.js`, which is the *token-gated protected-gallery* proxy, a different route from the public photos path the benchmark pages actually use — say which of the two is being measured rather than eliding them. **Path 2 (direct presigned R2 links) does not exist as a per-photo view path**: the signing primitive `S3StorageBackend.signedUrl` exists at `vendor/picpeak/backend/src/services/storage/S3StorageBackend.js:146`, but its only non-test caller is the download-all ZIP branch at `vendor/picpeak/backend/src/routes/gallery.js:904-916`, which is gated on `allow_presigned_download` **and** `storage.kind() === 's3'` **and** watermarking being off for the event, and 302-redirects a single ZIP object — not a photo, and not per photo. `LocalFsStorage.signedUrl` throws by design (`vendor/picpeak/backend/src/services/storage/LocalFsStorage.js:158`), so any measurement requires `STORAGE_BACKEND=s3`, which `docker-compose.yml:101-108` already sets for `backstage-backend`. The map therefore names the **smallest change that would make path 2 measurable end-to-end from the two AC-29.1.1 benchmark pages**, the exact files it would touch, whether it is additive to the fork (a `FORK_CHANGELOG.md`-class deviation) and a one-session yes/no estimate. It also names what such a path would give up, since the fork's own comment at `gallery.js:900-903` records that presigned bytes leave R2 unwatermarked and unlogged by the backend — that consequence is AC-29.5's problem, but it is discovered here. Evidence: the ADR subsection citing `file:line` for every claim, plus a Jest suite that asserts each cited file and symbol still exists at the pinned commit and that no per-photo presigned view route is present in `vendor/picpeak/backend/src/routes/` — an absence assertion over comment-stripped source, so the subsection's own prose cannot satisfy it.

The five discredited benchmark result files are withdrawn and the withdrawal is stated rather than silent. This criterion changes no application code, runs no browser, brings up no stack, builds no report and measures nothing — it is file removal plus one documentation line plus an absence test, and is separated from the origin fix (AC-29.2.2.1.2) and its live proof (AC-29.2.2.1.3) so that none of the three can be blocked by the others. The list is closed at exactly five files, each named and disqualified by AC-29.2.1. All five are committed on `feature/US-29` and none of them exist on `main`, so this work is done on the story branch: `scripts/benchmark/results/run-2026-08-08T14-51-01-229Z.json` and `run-2026-08-08T14-52-16-271Z.json`, added by `cb76fa3`, which recorded `transferBytes: 83` — the length of Express's `{"message":"Route not found"}` body and not a photograph; `run-2026-08-08T15-29-04-854Z-backstage-proxy.json` and `run-2026-08-08T15-30-06-730Z-backstage-proxy.json`, added by `a29a33a`, which carry a `deliveryPath` field the committed `scripts/benchmark/run.ts` cannot write, so no committed code reproduces them; and `scripts/benchmark/results/CANDIDATE_COVERAGE.md`, also from `a29a33a`, whose "Measured" claim cites two `presigned-r2` run files that do not exist. `scripts/benchmark/results/REPRODUCIBILITY.md` is **kept, not deleted**, and gains one line recording that its two runs were withdrawn and why, so the withdrawal is stated. AC-29.1.1's `scripts/benchmark/results/ac29.1.1-render-proof/` transcript and the directory's `.gitkeep` are untouched. The untracked `run-2026-08-08T16-*.json` files and `MEASURED_PATHS.md` currently sitting in the working tree are in the same category and are committed neither here nor anywhere — they were produced by wiring the `git reset --hard` to `ea49bf6` discarded, so no committed code reproduces them either. Because path 1 is then left with no surviving run, the unsplit AC-29.2.2's "cite the existing runs or re-run" conditional is settled here: path 1 is re-run, by AC-29.2.2.3. Evidence: a Jest suite asserting that none of the five named files remain under `scripts/benchmark/results/`, that `REPRODUCIBILITY.md` still exists and carries the withdrawal line, and that the `ac29.1.1-render-proof/` transcript survives intact.

Gallery image bytes are made to reach the browser from the Next.js page origin, by **committed** configuration, and that configuration is verified statically. This criterion runs no browser, brings up no stack, builds no report and measures nothing — the live proof is AC-29.2.2.1.3's; this criterion is done when the configuration is committed and a test over it is green. The gap is the one AC-29.2.1's map found and is confirmed to still hold: `next.config.ts` declares only `transpilePackages` and defines no `rewrites()` at all, so every gallery `` that the two `src/app/(frontend)/dev/benchmark-*-gallery` pages render 404s on the Next.js origin — which is why the runs withdrawn by AC-29.2.2.1.1 recorded `transferBytes: 83`. Close it by the mechanism candidate 1 actually names — the bytes reach the browser from the page origin and are served by the Backstage — which on a Next.js origin means a `rewrites()` entry in `next.config.ts` proxying the gallery image path prefix through to the Backstage backend; if the implementing session finds a mechanism that serves candidate 1 better, it may use it, but must name it in the commit message rather than substituting it silently. Two constraints are part of the criterion, not afterthoughts. First, the upstream is reached by Docker-network hostname — `backstage-backend` — and never `localhost` (CLAUDE.md Docker Rules): the destination is read from an environment variable whose value in `docker-compose.yml`'s `web-benchmark` block is that hostname, with `.env.example` documenting the variable if a new one is introduced. Second, the rewrite is scoped to the gallery image path prefix the benchmark pages actually emit, so it cannot shadow Next.js's or Payload's own `/api` routes. **It must be committed** — AC-29.2.1 disqualified the earlier runs precisely because nothing committed could reproduce them, so a working-tree-only fix fails this criterion outright. Evidence: a Jest suite over the committed configuration asserting that `next.config.ts` declares a `rewrites()`; that the declared source pattern matches the exact `/api/gallery/…` URL shape the pages emit, asserted against the URLs AC-29.1.1's committed render-proof transcript recorded rather than against a hand-written string; that the destination resolves to the `backstage-backend` Docker-network hostname; and that neither the config nor the compose value it reads contains `localhost`.

The origin fix is proven live, without Lighthouse: real image bytes are shown landing from the page origin, per image. With AC-29.2.2.1.2 committed, the Backstage stack up and the US-25 placement gallery seeded, an HTTP fetch of each of the two AC-29.1.1 benchmark routes returns HTML; every gallery `` in that HTML is then fetched individually; and each returns `200`, an `image/*` content type and a body far larger than the 83-byte 404 body the withdrawn runs measured. Per-image URL, HTTP status, content type and byte length are saved as a transcript under `scripts/benchmark/results/`, following the `ac29.1.1-render-proof/` convention already there, and **both the script and the transcript are committed**. Starting point, already untracked in the working tree, left by the session that hit the turn cap on 2026-08-08 — review and correct it rather than trust it: `scripts/ac29.2.2.1-benchmark-image-origin-proof.sh`, which mirrors `scripts/ac29.1.1-benchmark-render-proof.sh`'s convention, counts only `` elements whose `src` is a Backstage gallery URL so the shared site header's logo cannot pass the check, and fails any image that is not `200` **and** `image/*` **and** more than 83 bytes; and `scripts/benchmark/results/ac29.2.2.1-image-origin-proof/`, whose saved transcript records four `200` / `image/jpeg` / 7136-byte fetches across the two pages. That saved transcript is **not itself the evidence**: it was produced from wiring that was never committed, which is the same defect AC-29.2.1 used to disqualify the earlier runs. The run is repeated against the committed configuration and a freshly built `web-benchmark` service, and the regenerated transcript is what is committed. The one command that produces it is recorded in `BACKSTAGE_STARTUP.md`'s existing benchmark section, beside AC-29.1.3's. Bound: no Lighthouse is invoked and no report metric is produced (AC-29.2.2.3), no delivery-path switching is wired (AC-29.2.2.2), and no ADR prose is written (AC-29.3). Evidence: the committed proof script, its committed transcript showing every gallery image on both pages at `200`, `image/*` and well over 83 bytes, and the recorded command.

The delivery-path switch is wired so the harness can be pointed at either candidate and a report cannot be mislabelled. Still no Lighthouse and still no measurement. Starting point, committed at `ea49bf6` but deliberately unwired: `src/lib/benchmark/deliveryPathImages.ts` (a pure `applyDeliveryPath()` swap of the thumbnail/medium/large tiers), `resolveBenchmarkDeliveryPath.ts` (reads `BENCHMARK_DELIVERY_PATH` plus a generated URL map off disk), `redactSignedUrls.ts`, `observedDeliveryPath.ts`, and `scripts/benchmark/presign-r2-urls.sh`, which calls the fork's own `getStorage().signedUrl()` (`vendor/picpeak/backend/src/services/storage/S3StorageBackend.js:146`) inside the `backstage-backend` container and so adds no AWS SDK dependency to this repository; `.env.example` already documents the env var. Review and correct these rather than trusting them, and expect to redo work: the previous session's edits to tracked files were discarded by the `git reset --hard` to `ea49bf6` recorded in the reflog, and `src/__tests__/us29-ac29.2.1-candidate-mechanism-map.test.ts` deliberately pins the *unwired* state as ground truth, so its affected assertions are updated in this same commit with a one-line note naming the criterion that wired each thing — updated, never worked around or deleted wholesale. Wiring means: both benchmark pages apply the selected path; `scripts/benchmark/run.ts` writes the declared path into the report and **refuses to write a report whose observed image URLs contradict that label**; `docker-compose.yml`'s `web-benchmark` and `lighthouse-benchmark` blocks pass `BENCHMARK_DELIVERY_PATH` and mount the presign output; and `BACKSTAGE_STARTUP.md`'s benchmark section records the one command per path. Credential hygiene is part of this criterion, not an afterthought: `scripts/benchmark/presign-data/presigned-image-map.json` was committed at `a29a33a` carrying a live `X-Amz-Credential` access-key id and `X-Amz-Signature`, so generated presign output becomes gitignored and that file is removed from the working tree; committed reports keep the redaction already shown to work (`X-Amz-Credential=REDACTED`, `X-Amz-Signature=REDACTED`); and purging the blob from git history and rotating the key — a human decision — is raised as one item in `scrum-master/po-requests.md` in that file's existing format. Closing proof, without Lighthouse: with `BENCHMARK_DELIVERY_PATH=presigned-r2`, fetching each benchmark route returns HTML whose gallery `` values are all presigned `*.r2.cloudflarestorage.com` URLs, each fetching `200`, `image/*` and real bytes; with `backstage-proxy`, every one of the same images is served from the page origin instead. Both transcripts are saved beside AC-29.2.2.1's. If the presigned path cannot be made to serve real bytes end to end within this session, candidate 2 is **recorded as unmeasured with the specific blocking prerequisite named**, in exactly the form AC-29.2.3 requires of candidates 3–5, with one blocking entry in `po-requests.md` — never estimated, never extrapolated from candidate 1, never silently dropped. AC-29.2.1's one-session estimate for this change was *yes*, conditional on AC-29.2.2.1's origin gap being closed first, so that fallback is the exception and not the expectation. Evidence: a Jest suite over the pure modules — tier swap, redaction, and the mislabel refusal in particular — plus the two saved fetch transcripts.

The harness is run per candidate path and its labelled raw output is committed with the spread stated. This criterion produces numbers, nothing else. With AC-29.2.2.1 and AC-29.2.2.2 committed, the single command AC-29.1.3 recorded is run twice per measured path — that two-invocation rule is AC-29.1.3's, and is what makes a number reproducible rather than a sample — over both AC-29.1.1 pages, against the same production build and the same seeded US-25 placement gallery. Every raw run is retained and committed under `scripts/benchmark/results/`, and each report carries its candidate label both in its filename and in the `deliveryPath` field AC-29.2.2.2 made the harness write and verify, so a later reader cannot mistake which path a number came from. One summary is committed beside them stating, per path, per page and per metric — the four measurements the ADR commits to — the per-invocation medians and the spread between invocations, which is the noise floor AC-29.3 reads pass/fail against. That summary is generated from the retained reports, never hand-written: `scripts/benchmark/summarise-measurements.ts` and `src/lib/benchmark/invocationSpread.ts`, `loadRunReports.ts` and `measurementReport.ts` are already on disk untracked, left by the session that hit the turn cap on 2026-08-08 (`logs/20260808_201952_dev-team.json`, `terminal_reason: max_turns`), and are the starting point to review and correct rather than trust — while the eight `run-2026-08-08T16-*.json` files beside them predate the committed wiring, are not evidence, and are not committed. Any candidate this criterion does not measure is stated as unmeasured with its specific blocking prerequisite per AC-29.2.2.2's fallback; a path is never estimated, never extrapolated from the other, and never silently dropped. Bound: no ADR prose, no target restated, no per-target pass/fail, and no ranking or comparison between the two paths — AC-29.3 owns the write-up and AC-29.4 the decision, and candidates 3, 4 and 5 are AC-29.2.3's. Evidence: the committed raw reports and the generated summary, plus a Jest suite asserting that every committed report's filename label matches its `deliveryPath` field, that each number in the summary is re-derivable from the retained reports (the suite fails if summary and reports disagree), and that the summary introduces no target, pass/fail or ranking vocabulary.

The remaining three candidates are dispositioned — a closed set of exactly three, not an open survey. Candidate 3 (CDN / custom-domain public delivery), candidate 4 (edge authorisation Worker) and candidate 5 (hybrid) are each either measured or **explicitly recorded as unmeasured with its specific blocking prerequisite named**, in `R2_STORAGE_AND_DELIVERY_ADR.md` beside candidates 1 and 2. This sprint file's own `available_configuration` already records that paths 3 and 4 need infrastructure that does not exist, so recorded-unmeasured is the expected outcome and is a pass, not a failure — but the prerequisite must be concrete rather than generic: for 3, a Cloudflare custom domain or public bucket binding in front of the R2 bucket the AC-19.4 audit identified; for 4, a deployed Worker with an authorisation rule; for 5, both of those plus a decided rule for which galleries take which path, which is itself part of the AC-29.4 decision and so cannot precede it. Each distinct prerequisite is raised as one blocking item in `scrum-master/po-requests.md`, following that file's existing item format, and duplicates are consolidated rather than repeated per candidate. Evidence: a Jest suite asserting that the ADR's candidate section names all five candidates, that each carries exactly one disposition drawn from a closed vocabulary (measured / unmeasured-with-prerequisite), that every unmeasured disposition is followed by a named prerequisite and a matching `po-requests.md` entry, and that the ADR's standing rule at its lines 24-27 — that the candidates are 'listed to be measured, not ranked' — still stands, with no preference-based ranking language introduced ahead of AC-29.4's decision.

The measured numbers are written into `R2_STORAGE_AND_DELIVERY_ADR.md` per candidate path, replacing the `Status: UNDECIDED` block, with the raw harness output retained in the repository so the numbers can be re-derived rather than trusted. The four performance targets the ADR made itself accountable to are restated alongside the measurements, so pass/fail is visible per target per path.

The delivery-path decision is recorded and is made **from the measurements**: it names the chosen path, every rejected path, and for each rejection which of the four targets it missed and by how much. This is one of the decisions no agent may make alone (PRD §5, Reminder 1), so the record ends with an explicit Product Owner sign-off line and the decision is raised in `po-requests.md` if sign-off is not already recorded.

The chosen path is shown to preserve what PRD §19.3 requires of it — access control, logging, watermarks, and revocation where required. Concretely: a password-protected or unreleased gallery's image must not be fetchable without authorisation under the chosen path, proven by an unauthenticated request that is refused; and download/access logging still records a delivery. A faster path that leaks a private gallery fails this criterion outright.

If no candidate meets all four targets, the ADR says exactly that and the decision **stays open** with a named next step and its blocking prerequisite — rather than choosing the least-bad path and recording the targets as met. Sprint 3 recorded this decision as honestly UNDECIDED; closing it dishonestly would be worse than leaving it open a second sprint.

stories.dev_notes: AC-29.1.1 implemented (local checks green): All checks green. AC-29.1.1 is complete and committed. ## What was done The previous session's drafted work was on disk but unproven and partly wrong. I reviewed, corrected, ran the live proof, and committed it as `6df4887` on `feature/US-29`. **Two real defects found and fixed:** 1. **The proof script's pass condition was itself a false-green.** It counted *every* `` and required `> 1`.
